title: NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH HYPOTONIA, POOR GROWTH, DYSMORPHIC FACIES, AND AGAMMAGLOBULINEMIA

intro.text: This entry describes a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by hypotonia, poor growth, dysmorphic facial features, and agammaglobulinemia (NEDHGFA). I do not reliably remember the causal gene or the primary reports, so they are not stated here.

checks.claim: NEDHGFA is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly (Table 1).
checks.explanation: The paper describes hypotonia as part of the neurodevelopmental disorder.

checks.claim: NEDHGFA is characterized by poor growth.
checks.evidence_quote: They were unable to gain weight, had pale skin color, gradually developed cachexia, and had similar facial dysmorphisms, including triangle faces, big ears, etc.
checks.explanation: Patients could not gain weight and developed cachexia. Short stature is also reported.

checks.claim: NEDHGFA is characterized by dysmorphic facial features.
checks.evidence_quote: had similar facial dysmorphisms, including triangle faces, big ears, etc.
Five siblings from 2 consanguineous families in a large Slovakian family presented with developmental delay, neurological disorders, and agammaglobulinemia in childhood

paragraphs.text: NEDHGFA is a disorder of early childhood. Its cardinal features, as the title indicates, are global developmental delay and hypotonia, poor growth, dysmorphic facial features, and agammaglobulinemia with a B-cell deficiency that predisposes to recurrent infections. I do not remember the specific reports, the causal gene, or the mode of inheritance with enough confidence to give them.

checks.claim: NEDHGFA is a disorder of early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: These patients presented with not only ERAD-associated neurodevelopmental disorders with onset in infancy (ENDI) syndromes, but infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia with no mature B cells, resulting in frequent infections and early death.
checks.explanation: Onset is in infancy and patients died in early childhood.

checks.claim: Global developmental delay is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly (Table 1).
checks.explanation: The paper reports general developmental delay in all patients.

checks.claim: Hypotonia is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly (Table 1).
checks.explanation: The paper reports hypotonia in all patients.

checks.claim: Poor growth is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: They were unable to gain weight, had pale skin color, gradually developed cachexia
checks.explanation: Poor weight gain, cachexia and short stature are reported uniformly.

checks.claim: Dysmorphic facial features are a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: had similar facial dysmorphisms, including triangle faces, big ears, etc.
checks.explanation: The paper reports facial dysmorphisms in the patients.

checks.claim: Agammaglobulinemia is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical presentation was uniform among the 5 patients with ENDI-agammaglobulinemia (ENDI-A).
checks.explanation: Agammaglobulinemia is a defining feature and is part of the disorder's name.

checks.claim: The agammaglobulinemia in NEDHGFA occurs with a B-cell deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed no detectable mature CD19+ memory B cells in the circulation or circulating Igs at the age of 12 months and beyond (Table 2).
checks.explanation: The agammaglobulinemia occurs with an absence of mature B cells.

checks.claim: The B-cell deficiency in NEDHGFA predisposes patients to recurrent infections.
checks.evidence_quote: infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia with no mature B cells, resulting in frequent infections and early death.
checks.explanation: The paper says the B-cell deficiency led to frequent or recurrent infections.
